questions.text: What is the capital city of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: City of Manila. Not Quezon City, which is the most populous city.

questions.text: What is the largest island in the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Not Mindanao, which is second.

questions.text: What is the highest mountain in the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Apo, Bundok Apo.

questions.text: Which city is known as the "Summer Capital of the Philippines"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Baguio City.

questions.text: What famous cone-shaped hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season?
What small island in Aklan is famous for its powdery White Beach?
What ocean lies to the east of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Pacific. The Philippine Sea is the part of the Pacific next to the country; accept it too.

questions.text: Which city is known as the "Queen City of the South"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Cebu.

questions.text: The famous Puerto Princesa Underground River is in which province?
Which Mindanao city celebrates the Kadayawan Festival every August?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Davao.

questions.text: What river flows through Manila and empties into Manila Bay?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Pasig, Ilog Pasig.

questions.text: What Ilocos Sur city is famous for its cobblestone streets, calesas and Spanish-era houses?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Vigan City, Ciudad Fernandina. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.text: What is the largest lake in the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Laguna Lake, Lawa ng Laguna. Not Taal Lake or Lake Lanao.

questions.text: What body of water lies to the west of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: South China Sea. The West Philippine Sea is the Philippine name for the parts within its claimed waters.

questions.text: What large island lies just north of the Philippines, closest to its northern tip?
The Banaue Rice Terraces are in which province?
questions.hostNotes: Not Benguet or Mountain Province.

questions.text: Hundred Islands National Park, in Alaminos, is in which province?
Which Negros city, home of the MassKara Festival, is called the "City of Smiles"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Bacolod City.

questions.text: Which Mindanao city, where many people speak Chavacano, is called "Asia's Latin City"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Zamboanga.

questions.text: What is the northernmost province of the Philippines?
What is the longest river in the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Rio Grande de Cagayan. Not the Pasig River.

questions.text: What is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, running along eastern Luzon?
questions.hostNotes: Not the Cordillera Central, which is in northern Luzon.

questions.text: What bridge connects the islands of Samar and Leyte?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: San Juanico. It spans the San Juanico Strait.

questions.text: Which Leyte city was devastated by Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan) in 2013?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tacloban City.

questions.text: Which Mountain Province town is famous for its hanging coffins and caves?
Which Central Luzon province is called the "Rice Granary of the Philippines"?
questions.hostNotes: Not Isabela, another major rice producer.

questions.text: Siargao Island, home of the surf break Cloud 9, belongs to which province?
questions.hostNotes: Not Surigao del Sur.

questions.text: What island province, home of the Moriones Festival, is called the "heart of the Philippines"?
questions.hostNotes: It sits near the geographic center of the country and is roughly heart-shaped.

questions.text: Which Cordillera province, famous for La Trinidad's strawberry farms, is called the "Salad Bowl of the Philippines"?
What waterfall in Iligan City powers one of Mindanao's major hydroelectric plants?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Maria Cristina.

questions.text: What is the highest mountain in Luzon, famous for its "sea of clouds"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Pulag. It is the third-highest peak in the Philippines.

questions.text: What is the largest lake in Mindanao, on whose shore Marawi City stands?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Lanao, Ranao. It is the second-largest lake in the Philippines.

questions.text: Which Mindanao city is known as the "City of Golden Friendship"?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: CDO, Cagayan de Oro City.

questions.text: Which island province, famous for its Lanzones Festival, is called the "Island Born of Fire"?
What active volcano on Negros is the highest peak in the Visayas?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mount Kanlaon, Canlaon.

questions.text: Which city served as the official capital of the Philippines from 1948 to 1976?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: QC. Manila became the capital again in 1976.

questions.text: What is the third-largest island in the Philippines, after Luzon and Mindanao?
questions.hostNotes: Not Negros, which is fourth, or Palawan, which is fifth.

questions.text: Which Ilocos Norte town is known for the giant wind turbines lining its coast?
questions.hostNotes: The Bangui Wind Farm opened in 2005.

questions.text: What is the capital town of Batanes?
The Mangyan peoples are the indigenous groups of which large island?
The UNESCO-listed Tubbataha Reefs lie in the middle of which sea?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Sulu. Not the Celebes Sea.

questions.text: Lake Sebu, home of the T'boli people, is in which Mindanao province?
questions.hostNotes: Not Cotabato (North Cotabato) or Sultan Kudarat.

questions.text: What narrow strait separates the islands of Cebu and Negros?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Tanon Strait.

questions.text: What strait separates the northern Philippines from Taiwan?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Bashi Channel, which is part of it.

questions.text: What deep ocean trench runs just off the eastern coast of the Philippines?
questions.hostNotes: Also accept: Mindanao Trench, Philippine Deep. Not the Mariana Trench, which is farther east.
